analysis: The only change in this PR is a comment-only edit in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (head lines 4361-4363, around the sidecarsNeverStarveTheBlocks test). It reworded the explanation of SSDWriteBehind.consume's per-entry bucket charging, now saying that when the whole donation does not fit, entries are charged in array order. The patch has no executable changes, no assertions altered, and no production code touched. Related threat T-041 covers the encrypted SSD prefix cache (HMAC-keyed tags, TTL, endurance write cap, DBK3 AAD binding). The surrounding tests I examined cover the endurance cap, the sidecar header privacy commitment, TTL refresh and replay-bound behavior. Those tests are unchanged and still assert the same security-relevant invariants: no absolute token position in the plaintext header, the anti-splice commitment, and required blocks funded before optional sidecars. I identified no regression, new attack surface, or invalidated threat-model assumption. The head_text unit is a truncated excerpt (lines 1-609) and the base_text unit covers lines 4238-4588. The edited head lines are not visible in the head excerpt, but the patch hunk shows the change is comment-only. The actual SSDWriteBehind.consume implementation was not supplied, so the accuracy of the new comment is unverified. That is a documentation concern, not a security conclusion.
